The statute described, which is part of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA), establishes employer sanctions to prevent the employment of unauthorized aliens. Legally, this means that employers are prohibited from hiring, recruiting, or referring individuals for a fee if they know those individuals are not authorized to work in the United States. The legal implications of violating this provision include the imposition of significant civil fines and penalties. This framework places the burden on employers to verify the work authorization status of their employees, aiming to deter the hiring of undocumented workers through financial and legal consequences.
